# Objectives and Business Case

> Objectives and Business Case · 7 sections [loom:reference-model=core-architecture@1.0 2026-09-24T23:24:47.911Z youna.shin@ucdenver.edu]

# Strategic Context

*Name the strategy this work serves and the business capabilities it moves, so that everything below is traceable to something the organisation has already decided to care about. State what happens if the work is not done — the do-nothing option is the baseline every benefit in this document is measured against, and a document that never states it is arguing against an unnamed alternative.*

> **Recommended models:** ArchiMate Motivation View · Capability Map

# Objectives and Key Results

*State each objective as the change in the world you intend, not as the work you plan to do, and give it key results that are measurable, time-bound and owned. A key result that cannot go down as well as up is a task in disguise. Record the current baseline for every measure — without it there is no way to tell later whether the number moved because of this work or in spite of it.*

> **Recommended models:** OKR Trace Map

# Objective Alignment

*Show how these objectives roll up to the ones above them and what other work depends on the same outcomes. Where two objectives pull against each other — speed against reliability, reach against margin — say so here and say which one yields. Alignment recorded only as a list of parents is a claim; alignment recorded with its conflicts is a design.*

> **Recommended models:** OKR Trace Map · Capability Map

# Need and Approach

*State the need in the words of the person who has it, then the approach you propose to meet it, at the level of detail a sponsor can compare against an alternative. Keep the two separated: a need written in terms of the chosen solution has already smuggled the decision in, and once that happens the business case cannot be used to test the decision it exists to justify.*

> **Recommended models:** ArchiMate Motivation View · Capability Map

# Benefits, Costs and Financials

*List each benefit with its owner, its measure, and the date it is expected to land — a benefit nobody owns will not be claimed and cannot be checked. Set costs out over the same horizon, including the run cost that outlives the project, and state the confidence you have in each figure. Then give the summary numbers — total benefit, total cost, timeframe, NPV or IRR, ROI and breakeven — so the case can be compared with others on the same terms.*

> **Recommended models:** Cost / Capability Map · OKR Trace Map

# Alternatives, Assumptions and Risks

*Record the alternatives you considered and why each was set aside, including doing nothing and buying rather than building. State the assumptions the numbers rest on and what would falsify each one. Then the risks to the case itself — not the delivery risks, but the things that would make the benefits fail to appear even if the work ships exactly as planned.*

> **Recommended models:** Threat / Opportunity Matrix · Architecture Decision Record

# Value and Learning

*Say when the results will be reviewed, who reviews them, and what the review may change. Capture what was learned about the objective itself and not only about progress against it — the most valuable output of a measured objective is often the discovery that it was the wrong measure. Record that discovery here rather than quietly restating the target.*

> **Recommended models:** OKR Trace Map · SLO / Error Budget Table
